_note: Ground truth for M1. Medicare has no knee-specific MRI indications; coverage is governed by NCD 220.2 (Magnetic Resonance Imaging) general conditions, contraindications and non-covered uses. Rule code sets are provisional starter values to reconcile with Synthea coding in Phase 9.

criteria.text: The MRI is reasonable and necessary for the diagnosis or treatment of this patient and performed on an FDA-approved MRI unit.
criteria.source_quote: ...the services must be reasonable and necessary for the diagnosis or treatment of the specific patient involved.

criteria.text: The patient does not have metallic clips on vascular aneurysms (an MRI contraindication).
criteria.source_quote: MRI is not covered for patients with metallic clips on vascular aneurysms.

criteria.text: The MRI is not being performed during a viable pregnancy.
criteria.source_quote: MRI during a viable pregnancy. (listed among non-covered uses)

criteria.text: The study is not solely to image cortical bone or calcifications (a non-covered use).
criteria.source_quote: CMS has determined that MRI of cortical bone and calcifications... are therefore non-covered.

criteria.text: The patient can tolerate MRI (no uncontrolled claustrophobia and no ferromagnetic life-support/monitoring conflict).
criteria.source_quote: ...a history of claustrophobia unsuitable candidates for MRI procedures... the danger inherent in bringing ferromagnetic materials within range of MRI units...
